items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: First Coltrane, then it was a short while, he was replaced by Sonny Rollins. He was there briefly, then Coltrane [came] back.

ctx.x: So it was Beethoven‟s music? Was it the particular way of playing it? Or just the sound or both?

No, I think it was Beethoven‟s music. His music was … it‟s not quite … you know, I don‟t think [at] that particular time I didn‟t think anything the way I‟m analyzing today. Beethoven‟s music is more … [to] some degree, I think—this is probably a far- out analysis—but Coltrane, like, compared to Sonny Rollins … Sonny Rollins, if it was everyone like that, you might as well forget about it, or something. Certain things, Beethoven had certain things, more, try harder kind of things. Mozart, on the other hand, is…
Did you finish high school before your family emigrated to Japan?
